title: Scanning Probe Microscopy for Rheological Analysis of Biomolecular Condensates
author: Naghilou, Mashaghi

steps.title: Insert Cantilever into SPM Head
steps.instruction: Mount the glass cantilever holder on the mounting tool, loosen the top screw, place the cantilever chip under the metal clamp, straighten and secure it, then insert the holder into the SPM head, rotate 90°, and lock the tabs (≈5–10 min).

steps.title: Passivate Surfaces with BSA
steps.instruction: Prepare a fresh 10 mg/mL aqueous BSA solution and incubate each surface with excess solution to fully cover it; for polystyrene dishes incubate 30 min, for glass dishes first etch with 1 M NaOH for 1 h, wash, then incubate BSA 30 min, wash 5–6 times with dH₂O, and dry ≥4 h (use within 48 h).

substeps.instruction: Polystyrene: add BSA solution, cover surface, incubate 30 min.
Glass: etch silica with 1 M NaOH for 1 h, rinse with dH₂O, incubate BSA 30 min.
Wash all passivated surfaces 5–6 times with dH₂O.
Dry surfaces for at least 4 h; use within 48 h.

steps.title: Passivate Cantilever with Pluronic F127
steps.instruction: Prepare a fresh 1 % (w/v) aqueous Pluronic F127 solution, fill a culture dish (e.g., TPP) with it, withdraw 5 µL, hang the droplet from the pipette tip and place onto the cantilever without touching, immerse the cantilever by positioning the SPM head, incubate 30 min, rinse gently with dH₂O, then place the head in a fresh dH₂O bath for another 30 min (avoid air bubbles; reuse cantilever with regular re‑passivation).

substeps.instruction: Make 1 % (w/v) Pluronic F127 solution.
Fill measurement dish with solution.
Withdraw 5 µL, hang droplet from tip, deposit onto cantilever.
Position SPM head to immerse cantilever, incubate 30 min.
Rinse cantilever with dH₂O, avoiding tip damage.
Soak head in fresh dH₂O for 30 min.

steps.title: Prepare Condensate Mixture
steps.instruction: On a BSA‑coated surface add the following volumes to obtain the listed final concentrations (total ≥40 µL): 10 µL 4 M KCl → 1 M final, 4 µL 100 mM imidazole → 10 mM, 0.8 µL 0.5 % w/v NaN₃ → 0.01 % w/v, 20 µL 100 g/L Ficoll PM70 → 50 g/L, 1.6 µL 1 M heparin → 40 µM, 1.14 µL 1.4 M poly‑L‑lysine → 40 µM, and 2.46 µL dH₂O; mix gently, first the buffer components, then add heparin, finally poly‑L‑lysine, observing a milky suspension.

substeps.instruction: Add KCl, imidazole, NaN₃, and Ficoll to reach working buffer.
Gently mix, then add heparin.
Add poly‑L‑lysine last; mix gently to obtain milky suspension.

steps.title: Allow Condensate Droplets to Settle
steps.instruction: Let the droplets rest on the dish for approximately 2 h until coalescence events cease before SPM measurement (critical: sample volume ≥40 µL; wear PPE when handling NaN₃).

steps.title: Measure Droplet Radius via ImageJ
steps.instruction: Capture an image of each droplet and use ImageJ (or similar) to determine its radius.

steps.title: Export SPM Data to Text Files
steps.instruction: In JPK data‑processing software use Batch Processing to export each measurement as a .txt file, ensuring the columns: Vertical tip position, Vertical deflection, Height, Height (measured and smoothed), Height (measured), Series time, and Segment time are included.

steps.title: Perform Phase Calibration Using Notebook
steps.instruction: Open the Mathematica notebook Biomolecular_Condensate_Rheology_v2.nb, set the variable `filename` to the empty‑surface .txt file, run the notebook to obtain the list of φ (Arg(X)) versus frequency f, import φ(f) into a data‑analysis tool (e.g., Origin), and linearly fit the data (average multiple φ(f) curves before fitting if desired).

steps.title: Calculate Complex Shear Modulus
steps.instruction: In the same notebook input the fitted slope and intercept as `phaseSlope` and `phaseOffset`, set `particleRadius` to the measured droplet radius, enable `compensateSurfaceEnergy`, choose a touchdown mode (`snap` or `hard`) and specify the corresponding parameters (snapFilterLength, snapKeepout, snapBaselineLength or hardLength), then run the program to generate G.dat (complex shear modulus vs frequency) and surface‑energy data.

substeps.instruction: Set phaseOffset and phaseSlope from φ(f) fit.
Enter particleRadius.
Enable surface energy compensation.
Select touchdown mode:
Snap – define snapFilterLength, snapKeepout, snapBaselineLength.
Hard – define hardLength.
Run notebook to produce G.dat and surface‑energy output.

steps.title: Determine Viscosity from G″ Data
steps.instruction: Load the G″ column from G.dat into a data‑analysis tool, perform a linear fit of G″ versus frequency, and take the slope as the condensate viscosity.
